These fixtures use `{"filename": ...}`, which matches the buggy reader in `infer_pr_complexity_fallback` but **not** the production `PRContext.changed_files` shape (`{"path": ...}` from `fetch_pr_context`).

That is why `test_runtime_path_is_high` / `test_docs_only_is_low` stay green while real runs never see path markers. Build fixtures with `"path"` (and ideally one case that would fail if the reader still used `filename`).

The new agent-runner bridge is documented, but the **diff-based heuristic fallback** (CHANGELOG + `infer_pr_complexity_fallback`) is not. Consumers reading this page still think labels only come from `set_pr_complexity` / `findings.json` complexity, and the “why not just count lines?” section is now incomplete: when the model omits a level, labeling *does* fall back to path markers + file/line counts.

Please document when the fallback runs, that it is best-effort, and that an explicit model level always wins.

Even after fixing the `path` key, this fallback ranks primarily by `len(paths)` and `additions+deletions`, which collides with the product promise that complexity labels are **not** line-count based (`docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md` § “Why not just count lines?”, README feature blurb).

Path markers help, but any multi-file or >100-line PR without those substrings becomes `medium`/`high` purely from size. Prefer keeping fallback conservative (`low` unless a high-signal marker matches) or document clearly that fallback is size-biased and only a last resort when the model omits a level.

**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

`fetch_pr_context` stores each changed file as `{"path": f.get("filename", ...), ...}`, but this fallback reads `f.get("filename")`. On every real run `paths` is a list of empty strings, so high-path markers never fire and docs-only detection never sees `.md` suffixes — only the crude `len(paths)` / `line_delta` branches remain.

That breaks the advertised safety net whenever the model omits `complexity` (common on agent-runners). Read `path` (optionally keep `filename` as a legacy alias).

```suggestion
    paths: list[str] = [
        str(f.get("path") or f.get("filename") or "") for f in pr_ctx.changed_files
    ]
```

## Verdict

Solid feature direction — complexity labeling on agent-runners via `findings.json` is the right bridge — but **do not merge until the heuristic fallback key bug is fixed**. Production `PRContext.changed_files` never carries `filename`, so the new safety net is largely dead on real runs.

## Narrative

### What works
- Provider plumbing looks correct: `require_complexity_in_findings` flows through Claude Code / Cursor / Codex into `write_findings_prompt_directive`, `ReviewResult.complexity` is parsed, and `resolve_pr_complexity` prefers chat-completions `set_pr_complexity` over findings.json.
- `build_agent_runner_noop_warning` correctly stops treating complexity as a CLI no-op; autocomplete remains the only warned gap.
- Docs/matrix updates in `PROVIDERS.md`, setup reference, README feature blurb, CHANGELOG, and self-review dogfood (`complexity-labels-enabled: true`, gate label `ready`) are coherent with the runtime intent.
- Self-review label rename `AIReview` → `ready` matches `AGENTS.md` / `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md` (already documented as `ready`).

### Blocking issue
`infer_pr_complexity_fallback` reads `f.get("filename")`, but `fetch_pr_context` normalizes GitHub’s API field into **`path`**. On real PRs every path becomes `""`, so:
- `scripts/reviewer.py` / `action.yml` / `auth` markers never match → no forced `high`
- single-doc `.md` detection never matches → no forced `low`
- only empty-path count + `additions+deletions` remain

The new unit tests construct fixtures with `filename`, so they **encode the bug** and stay green. Fix the reader to use `path` (and update fixtures to the production shape).

### Other notes
- Document the heuristic fallback in `docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md` (CHANGELOG already advertises it; the user-facing page does not).
- Even after the key fix, size thresholds quietly reintroduce line-count labeling contrary to the “not line-count based” product promise — keep fallback conservative or document the bias.
- JSON schema place
